source_records.source_title: ChatGPT was down for many — as OpenAI says it's 'monitoring the recovery'

summary: On 20 April 2026, an internal OpenAI authentication service became overloaded after a temporary backend disruption, reducing ChatGPT availability and causing login or signup failures across ChatGPT, Codex and platform.openai.com. OpenAI reported that retry, caching and routing behaviour amplified the overload and that some ordinary backend availability errors unnecessarily sent users into login flows. Authentication substantially recovered within about 82 minutes and overall ChatGPT metrics within about 102 minutes.

primary_classification.classification_basis: Backend availability errors unnecessarily triggered login flows, collapsing a service-availability cause into an authentication-state representation with the wrong recovery path.

assessment_boundaries: The provider-attributed root cause and remediation are accepted as first-party reporting, not independently verified internal telemetry.
Downdetector volumes and reader polls are self-reported signals and are not converted into a verified affected-user population.
The classification rests on the provider's disclosed misrepresentation of backend availability errors through login flows, not on multi-surface outage symptoms alone.
The evidence does not establish loss or deletion of conversation content, financial loss, essential-service collapse or other downstream harm.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI reports that an internal authentication-edge dependency overloaded after a temporary backend disruption. Retry, caching and routing behaviour amplified the load and impeded graceful recovery. Some users experienced ChatGPT errors or login and signup failures across ChatGPT, Codex and platform.openai.com, and backend availability errors unnecessarily triggered login flows. Authentication recovered by about 08:20 PDT, ChatGPT edge availability by about 08:40, and overall ChatGPT metrics by about 09:00.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The decisive governance failure was not merely reduced availability. The system converted one operational cause—backend availability failure—into a different user-facing state—login required. That representation could direct users toward credential or account recovery when the corrective action belonged to provider-side service recovery. Access-state integrity requires those causes and recovery routes to remain distinguishable even during overload.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This incident demonstrates that resilience controls and state representation are coupled. Load shedding, circuit breakers, cache policy and routing must prevent overload amplification, while error handling must preserve the distinction between unavailable service and invalid authentication. The published mechanism satisfies Access-State Differentiation without treating every authentication-adjacent outage as that class.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Translate the provider's post-incident mechanism and prevention statements into the governing access-state invariant and current taxonomy boundary.

clauses.source_paraphrase: OpenAI attributes the disruption to overload in an authentication-edge dependency and says retry, caching and routing behaviour amplified the overload and prevented graceful recovery.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Critical authentication paths require sufficient headroom and bounded retry, caching, routing, load-shedding and failover behaviour so a temporary backend failure does not cascade into broader access loss.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The overload explains why access failed, but the mapping in this row depends on the provider's separate statement that availability errors were represented through unnecessary login flows. Generic overload alone would not establish the represented-state mismatch.

clauses.source_paraphrase: OpenAI says backend availability errors should be surfaced appropriately and should not unnecessarily trigger login flows.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Service unavailability and invalid or expired authentication are materially different access causes and must be represented with distinct recovery routes wherever the difference affects correct continuation.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Backend availability errors unnecessarily triggered login flows, collapsing a service-availability cause into an authentication-state representation with the wrong recovery path.

No expiry, revocation, refresh, recovery or credential-replacement transition is shown to have propagated incoherently to an active session; the published defect is misrepresentation of an availability error.
An authentication-edge dependency was overloaded, but the evidence does not establish the class's otherwise-valid entitlement, inconclusive verifier and no-proportionate-fallback conditions.
